1	; This script is intended for indirect use via commands registered by install.ahk.
2	; It can also be compiled as a replacement for AutoHotkey.exe, so tools which run
3	; scripts by executing AutoHotkey.exe can benefit from automatic version selection.
4	#requires AutoHotkey v2.0
5	
6	;@Ahk2Exe-SetDescription AutoHotkey Launcher
7	#SingleInstance Off
8	#NoTrayIcon
9	
10	#include inc\identify.ahk
11	#include inc\launcher-common.ahk
12	#include inc\ui-base.ahk
13	
14	if A_ScriptFullPath == A_LineFile || A_LineFile == '*#1' {
15	    SetWorkingDir A_InitialWorkingDir
16	    Main
17	}
18	
19	Main() {
20	    switches := []
21	    while A_Args.length {
22	        arg := A_Args.RemoveAt(1)
23	        if SubStr(arg,1,1) != '/' {
24	            ScriptPath := arg
25	            break
26	        }
27	        nextArgValue() {
28	            if !A_Args.Length {
29	                MsgBox "Invalid command line switches; missing value for " arg ".", "AutoHotkey Launcher", "icon!"
30	                ExitApp 1
31	            }
32	            return A_Args.RemoveAt(1)
33	        }
34	        switch arg, false {
35	        case '/RunWith':    ; Launcher-specific
36	            A_Args.runwith := nextArgValue()
37	        case '/Launch':     ; Launcher-specific
38	            A_Args.launch := true
39	        case '/Which':
40	            A_Args.which := true
41	            if trace.Enabled
42	                trace.DefineProp 'call', {call: (this, s) => OutputDebug(s "`n")} ; Don't use stdout.
43	        case '/iLib', '/include':
44	            switches.push(arg)
45	            switches.push(nextArgValue())
46	        default:
47	            switches.push(arg)
48	        }
49	        
50	    }
51	    if !IsSet(ScriptPath)
52	        && !FileExist(ScriptPath := A_ScriptDir "\AutoHotkey.ahk")
53	        && !FileExist(ScriptPath := A_MyDocuments "\AutoHotkey.ahk")
54	        && !FileExist(ScriptPath := A_ScriptDir "\ui-dash.ahk") {
55	        ExitApp
56	    }
57	    if ScriptPath = '*'
58	        ExitApp 2 ; FIXME: code would need to be read in and then passed to the real AutoHotkey
59	    IdentifyAndLaunch ScriptPath, A_Args, switches
60	}
61	
62	GetLaunchParameters(ScriptPath, interactive:=false) {
63	    code := FileRead(ScriptPath, 'UTF-8')
64	    require := prefer := rule := exe := ""
65	    if RegExMatch(code, 'im)^[ `t]*#Requires[ `t]+AutoHotkey[ `t]+([^;`r`n]*?)[ `t]*(?:;[ `t]*prefer[ `t]+([^;`r`n\.]+))?(?:$|;)', &m) {
66	        trace "![Launcher] " m.0
67	        require := RegExReplace(m.1, '[^\s,]\K\s+(?!$)', ",")
68	        prefer := RegExReplace(m.2, '[^\s,]\K\s+(?!$)', ",")
69	        rule := "#Requires"
70	    }
71	    else if ConfigRead('Launcher', 'Identify', true) {
72	        i := IdentifyBySyntax(code)
73	        trace "![Launcher] syntax says version " (i.v || "unknown") " -- " i.r
74	        if i.v
75	            require := String(i.v)
76	        rule := i.r
77	        if rule = "error"
78	            MsgBox "Syntax detection has failed due to an error in the launcher.`n`n" Type(i.err) ": " i.err.Message " " i.err.Extra "`n`n"
79	                . "Character index " i.pos "`n" SubStr(code, i.pos, 50) "`n...`n`n"
80	                . "Please report this on the forums, with sample code that triggers the error.", "AutoHotkey Launcher", "icon!"
81	    }
82	    else {
83	        trace "![Launcher] version unknown - syntax-checking is disabled"
84	    }
85	    if !(hasv := RegExMatch(require, '(^|,)\s*(?!(32|64)-bit)[<>=]*v?\d')) {
86	        ; No version specified or detected
87	        if hasv := v := ConfigRead('Launcher', 'Fallback', "") {
88	            require .= (require=''?'':',') v
89	            trace "![Launcher] using fallback version " v
90	        }
91	    }
92	    v := GetVersionToInstall(require) ; Currently used for multiple purposes
93	    if !hasv
94	        exe := interactive ? PromptMajorVersion(ScriptPath, require, prefer) : ""
95	    else
96	        if !exe := GetRequiredOrPreferredExe(require, prefer)
97	            if interactive {
98	                if v && !LocateExeByVersion(v, '')
99	                    exe := TryToInstallVersion(v, rule, ScriptPath, require, prefer)
100	                else
101	                    RequirementNotMetMsgBox require, ScriptPath
102	            }
103	    lp := {exe: exe, id: exe ? GetMajor(exe.Version) : GetLikelyMajor(require), v: v, switches: []}
104	    if exe {
105	        if GetMajor(exe.Version) = 1 && ConfigRead('Launcher\v1', 'UTF8', false)
106	            lp.switches.Push('/CP65001')
107	    }
108	    return lp
109	}
110	
111	ParseRequiresVersion(s) {
112	    return RegExMatch(s, 'i)^(?!(?:32|64)-bit$)(?<op>[<>=]*)v?(?<version>(?<major>\d+)\b\S*)', &m) ? m : 0
113	}
114	
115	GetLikelyMajor(r) {
116	    if IsNumber(r)
117	        return Integer(r)
118	    ; Usually there would be either a version number with no operator
119	    ; or a range where the lower and upper bound have the same major.
120	    Loop Parse r, ",", " `t"
121	        if (m := ParseRequiresVersion(A_LoopField)) && m.op != '<'
122	            return m.major
123	    return ''

; Run this script to launch or download and install Ahk2Exe into A_ScriptDir '\..\Compiler'.
#requires AutoHotkey v2.0

#include install.ahk
#include inc\GetGitHubReleaseAssetURL.ahk

#SingleInstance Force
InstallAhk2Exe

InstallAhk2Exe() {
    inst := Installation()
    inst.ResolveInstallDir()  ; This sets inst.InstallDir and inst.UserInstall
    
    finalPath := inst.InstallDir '\Compiler\Ahk2Exe.exe'
    if FileExist(finalPath) {
        ShellRun finalPath
        ExitApp
    }
    
    if !A_Args.Length {
        (inst.UserInstall) || SetTimer(() => (
            WinExist('ahk_class #32770 ahk_pid ' ProcessExist()) &&
            SendMessage(0x160C,, true, 'Button1') ; BCM_SETSHIELD := 0x160C
        ), -25)

# Build and install on Arch Linux:  makepkg -si   (run in this folder)
pkgname=autohotkey-ux
pkgver=2.0.19
pkgrel=1
pkgdesc="AutoHotkey Dash, New Script, Launch/Editor settings and Window Spy for KDE Plasma"
arch=('x86_64')
license=('GPL-2.0-or-later')
depends=('gcc-libs' 'glibc' 'libxkbcommon' 'wayland' 'libx11' 'libglvnd' 'xdg-utils' 'xdg-desktop-portal')
optdepends=(
  'wine: run AutoHotkey scripts and Ahk2Exe'
  'kdotool: Window Spy on KDE Plasma (Wayland)'
  'xdotool: Window Spy on X11'
  'xorg-xprop: window class in Window Spy on X11'
  'imagemagick: pixel colour in Window Spy on X11'
  'kdialog: launcher error messages'
  'noto-fonts: the intended UI font'
)
makedepends=('cargo')
source=()

build() {
  cd "$startdir"
  cargo build --release --locked
}

package() {
  cd "$startdir"
  install -Dm755 target/release/autohotkey-ux "$pkgdir/usr/bin/autohotkey-ux"
  install -Dm644 packaging/autohotkey-ux-dash.desktop "$pkgdir/usr/share/applications/autohotkey-ux-dash.desktop"
  install -Dm644 packaging/autohotkey-ux-spy.desktop "$pkgdir/usr/share/applications/autohotkey-ux-spy.desktop"
  install -Dm644 packaging/autohotkey.xml "$pkgdir/usr/share/mime/packages/autohotkey-ux.xml"
  install -Dm644 packaging/autohotkey-new.desktop "$pkgdir/usr/share/templates/autohotkey-new.desktop"
  install -Dm644 packaging/template.ahk "$pkgdir/usr/share/templates/.source/AutoHotkey Script.ahk"
}

# AutoHotkey Dash for Linux (Rust)

A Rust/egui rebuild of AutoHotkey's UX tools (the Dash, New Script, Launch
settings, Editor settings, Window Spy and the version launcher), made for Arch
Linux with KDE Plasma. AutoHotkey itself is a Windows program, so scripts and
Ahk2Exe run through **Wine**.

## Install on Arch

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel rust wine
makepkg -si            # in this folder
```

Optional: `kdotool` (AUR, Window Spy on Wayland), `xdotool xorg-xprop imagemagick`
(Window Spy on X11), `kdialog`.

Put an AutoHotkey install where the app can find it (any of):
`~/.local/share/AutoHotkey`, `~/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/AutoHotkey`,
`/opt/autohotkey`, or set `AHK_ROOT=/path/to/AutoHotkey`. It should contain
`v2/AutoHotkey64.exe` (and optionally `v1.1.x/`, `Compiler/Ahk2Exe.exe`, `UX/installed-files.csv`).

## Use

| Command | What it opens |
|---|---|
| `autohotkey-ux` | the Dash |
| `autohotkey-ux --new [folder/or/file.ahk]` | New Script |
| `autohotkey-ux --launch-config` | Launch settings |
| `autohotkey-ux --editor` | Editor settings |
| `autohotkey-ux --spy` | Window Spy |
| `autohotkey-ux --run script.ahk [args]` | run a script with the right AutoHotkey version |
| `autohotkey-ux --edit script.ahk` | open a script in your chosen editor |
| `autohotkey-ux --install-desktop` | make .ahk files open with the launcher |

Settings live in `~/.config/autohotkey-ux/config.json` (the original used the
Windows registry under `HKCU\Software\AutoHotkey`).

content.text:
I rebuilt the AutoHotkey Dash in Rust, with the same windows as the original: the main Dash menu, New Script, Launch settings, Editor settings, Window Spy, and the "Run script with…" version picker. The layout, sizes, colours and wording come from the original, which I photographed and compared side by side. It builds and passes the automatic check. The Linux version compiles cleanly, but I haven't run it on a real Arch/KDE machine, so the Linux-only parts below are untested.

To make it work on Arch with KDE:
- **Settings** are saved to a settings file in your home folder instead of the Windows registry.
- **Running scripts and the compiler:** AutoHotkey and its script compiler are Windows programs, so they run through Wine.
- **Opening .ahk files:** the app registers itself so Dolphin opens `.ahk` files through it. It picks the correct AutoHotkey version for each script; I confirmed it chooses the right one for both a v1 and a v2 script.
- **Editors** are your installed KDE text editors (Kate, KWrite and so on).
- **Install files:** I included a package recipe for one-command installation on Arch.

What differs or is still unverified:
- **Window Spy:** KDE on Wayland limits what one program can see of others. It needs small helper tools (kdotool on Wayland, xdotool on X11) and shows less than the original: no status-bar or control text, and the colour under the mouse only works on X11.
- **Help:** the help links open the online documentation, because Linux can't open pages inside the offline help file.
- **Icons:** they are simple drawn stand-ins rather than the Windows ones, and the font is the closest Linux equivalent.
- **Version guessing:** for scripts without a "#Requires" line, guessing the version from the code is a simplified version of the original's method.

You told me to decide on the open questions myself, so I did. Since Window Spy can't work fully on Wayland, I made it show what it can and leave the rest empty rather than dropping it. For version guessing, I used a simpler method that follows the same rule as the original.

A good next step would be to install it on your Arch machine and tell me how Window Spy and double-clicking `.ahk` files behave there, so I can fix anything KDE-specific.
